chunks: Had there been gods apart from God, both (the heavens and the earth) would have been despoiled. Much too glorious is God, the Lord of the mighty throne, for things they assert!
ai.seo_question: What is the argument for divine unity in Surah Al-Anbiya regarding the order of the universe?
ai.summary: In Shia tafsir, this verse is often cited as a rational proof (dalil aqli) for the necessity of a single, unique Creator, emphasizing that multiplicity in divinity would lead to cosmic chaos (fasad). It underscores the attribute of Allah as Al-Wahid (The One) and Al-Ahad (The Unique), distinguishing Him from the polytheistic view of multiple independent deities. The glorification at the end serves to negate any anthropomorphic or pluralistic attributes ascribed to God by the mushrikeen.
